channel.title: Counter Space
channel.description: Kitchen gear, judged by what it does on a Tuesday night.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: They share a name and almost nothing else. The decision is not about which fries better — it is about how you cook on a normal weeknight.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Quarts are the least honest number on the box. Here is what to check instead, and why the biggest number is often the wrong buy.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: The appliance you stop using is the one that is annoying to wash. This is the least glamorous part of the decision and the most predictive.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: Every appliance claims ten jobs. The useful question is which two it does well, and whether those two are the jobs you have.

item.title: Instant-read or wireless: which meat thermometer fits your grill?
item.description: One answers "is this done right now?". The other answers "tell me when it is done" while the lid stays shut. The right one depends on how you cook.

item.title: Seven places an air fryer quietly beats a second oven
item.description: A working list of the jobs a basket or countertop unit does better than heating the big oven — reheating, small batches, and everything you would rather not wait twenty minutes for.

item.title: Cooking two holiday dishes at once: the two-temperature problem
item.description: Holiday cooking is a scheduling problem, not a recipe problem. When the oven is full, the second dish needs its own chamber — and its own clock.
